no-priors.name: No Priors
no-priors.bio: Podcast: Rethinking Legacy Data Infrastructure with Eon Co-Founders Ofir Ehrlich and Gonen Stein

html_en:
The agent economy is arriving faster than the infrastructure to support it — and the gap between "agents can do things" and "the world is ready for agents doing things" is widening by the day.

🤖 The Agentic Internet Nobody Built For

Box CEO Aaron Levie put his finger on something important this week:

"The internet is almost entirely unprepared for a future where everyone's personal agents are running around executing tasks for them. There are going to be endless new challenges and opportunities at the infrastructure layer, for user experiences, new business models, and more." — @levie

It's a deceptively simple observation with enormous implications. We've spent three decades building the web for human users — with human-paced interactions, human-readable interfaces, and human-scale security assumptions. Autonomous agents blow up every one of those assumptions simultaneously. The Eon co-founders, speaking on No Priors, framed the security dimension with particular clarity:

"Up until now, the concerns came from human threats. What we're seeing now on steroids is that the same type of threat is coming from nonhuman actors, agents that essentially have legitimate access to the environment with legitimate permissions... but the velocity of that happening is extreme." — Ofir Ehrlich, No Priors

The scarier version of this problem isn't the malicious agent — it's the well-intentioned one operated by someone who doesn't know what they're doing. As Eon co-founder Gonen Stein noted:

"Think of the nontechnical people. They're not even aware for things like security or compliance or who is gonna use this data. Maybe their agent that they are building are using other agents, and they're not technical to even understand what it means. It creates a complete set of actors inside the organization, not bound by the rules of the organization... handling sensitive data." — Gonen Stein, No Priors

There's a counterpoint worth noting. @zarazhangrui raised a quieter, more humanistic concern: "One of the biggest crises of our time is the shortening of the human attention span. Agents just make things worse." As we delegate more cognitive tasks, the question of what we're actually optimizing for deserves more airtime.

💾 Data Is Finally, Actually the Moat

People have been calling data "the new oil" for so long the metaphor had gone stale. Then Google quietly bought Spirit Airlines' customer dataset out of bankruptcy for $10 million — and the cliché snapped back into focus.

"They didn't buy airplanes. They bought the data... for $10,000,000 because they think it's very important in that perspective. They're using it to train models." — Gonen Stein, No Priors

The No Priors host added a detail that makes the story even richer: apparently Mercor was the competing bidder in the bankruptcy process. So you had two AI-era companies — one from Google, one a hiring platform — fighting over a defunct airline's enterprise dataset. Watch/Listen: Rethinking Legacy Data Infrastructure with Eon Co-Founders

Eon's founders argue this is the beginning of a structural trend. Models, compute, tooling — all of it is commoditizing fast. What can't be replicated is a company's accumulated operational history.

"Everyone has access to all of those cool new tools. The only real advantage that companies have today is, of course, their people, but also the data that they've accrued. Because everyone has access to all of those cool new tools... data becomes the moat." — Gonen Stein, No Priors

And the Spirit dataset itself? The hypothesis is that dense, real-world enterprise dialogue data — customer support transcripts, internal communications, operational records — is exactly what agent builders need and can't easily synthesize. Lab-generated training data looks too clean. Real companies are messy, and that messiness is the point.

📋 Footnotes & Ambient Signal

A lighter moment in the feed: @petergyang cheekily noted that a certain prominent voice calling AGI wasn't on Time's 100 Top AI list — the "/s" doing heavy lifting there. @thenanyu logged it simply as "J-dog calling AGI," which at this point reads less like news and more like a recurring calendar event.

Meanwhile, in a small but telling sign of the times, @nikunj flagged that Fable's AI is now reviewing every code change from Astra's engineering team — and apparently has opinions. "This fix is the real deal," it reportedly declared. AI as code reviewer, critic, and collaborator: normalized, apparently.
html_zh:
AI智能体时代正在悄然重塑企业的每一个层面——从数据基础设施的价值重估，到互联网安全架构的全面挑战，这场变革比大多数人意识到的来得更快、更深。

🤖 智能体的崛起：互联网还没准备好

Box CEO Aaron Levie 本周发出了一个值得认真对待的警告：

"互联网几乎完全没有为未来做好准备——在那个未来里，每个人的个人智能体都在四处奔跑、执行任务。在基础设施层、用户体验、新商业模式等方面，将会涌现无穷无尽的新挑战与新机遇。"
—— @levie

这不是泛泛而谈。当数以亿计的AI智能体开始代表用户自主行动，现有的身份验证体系、权限管理和数据安全框架都是为"人类操作者"设计的——它们根本没有考虑过非人类行为者的存在。

不过，也有人对智能体的普及持更为审慎的态度。@zarazhangrui 指出了一个更深层的社会隐忧：

"我们这个时代最大的危机之一，是人类注意力持续时间的不断缩短。智能体只会让事情变得更糟。"

效率与认知退化之间的张力，将是未来几年难以回避的辩题。

🔒 数据安全的新战场：当"合法身份"成为威胁

Watch/Listen: No Priors — Rethinking Legacy Data Infrastructure with Eon Co-Founders

在 No Priors 播客中，云备份与数据恢复公司 EON 的联合创始人 Ofir Ehrlich 和 Gonen Stein 描述了一种令人不安的新型安全威胁：

"此前，威胁主要来自人类攻击者。而我们现在看到的，是同样类型的威胁被极度放大——来自非人类行为者，即那些以合法身份、合法权限进入系统的智能体。我们在检测和防护方面的方法论是相似的，但这件事发生的速度极为惊人。"
—— Ofir Ehrlich，EON 联合创始人

更令人担忧的，是组织内部"全民皆可构建"带来的失控风险：

"想想那些非技术人员。他们甚至没有意识到安全、合规或数据使用的问题。他们构建的智能体可能在调用其他智能体，而他们根本不理解这意味着什么。这在组织内部创造了一整套不受组织规则约束、未必在组织内部运行、却在处理敏感数据的行为者群体。"
—— Gonen Stein，EON 联合创始人

💰 数据即黄金：从破产航空公司身上，读懂AI时代的资产逻辑

本期播客中最引人注目的案例，莫过于 Google 从破产的 Spirit Airlines 手中购买数据集——而且据悉，另一个竞标方是招聘AI公司 Mercor。

"两天前，你看到 Google 从破产的 Spirit Airlines 那里买了些东西。他们买的不是飞机——他们买的是数据。他们花了1000万美元买数据，因为他们认为这非常重要。他们用它来训练模型。"
—— Gonen Stein

这个细节耐人寻味：两家AI公司同时竞拍一家破产航空公司的企业数据集。Stein 进一步解释了这一趋势背后的逻辑：

"如果你今天是一家科技数据公司的CEO，我可以告诉你，你会不断收到这样的问题：'你愿意出售你的数据吗？'……模型、算力，一切都相对短暂，几乎没有转换成本。但如果你是一家酒店集团、餐饮集团或科技公司，你拥有的最有价值的东西，其实是你的数据。"

"数据是新石油"这句话喊了十年，终于在大模型后训练时代找到了真实的兑现路径。当所有公司都能用上同样的工具和模型，数据才是真正的护城河。

🏆 边角料：AGI宣言与榜单政治

AI圈从不缺少戏剧性时刻。@thenanyu 简短地发推："J-dog 宣称AGI已至"——所指似乎是某位业内人士对AGI到来时间线的又一次预测，引发社区一片调侃。

与此同时，@petergyang 用反讽的语气回应了 Time 百大AI人物榜单的权威性问题：

"这个人甚至没上 Time 百大AI榜单，我们为什么要听他的？/s"

榜单即权威，权威即流量——这大概是AI媒体生态的另一面镜子。
